summary: A 1935 CCC-built steel lookout on Cove Mountain in Great Smoky Mountains National Park, now an NPS air-quality station that visitors cannot enter.

facts.design: 60-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 ft metal cab

access.note: Summit reachable on foot; hikers are not allowed into the tower (per the Hiking in the Smokys guide); the NPS uses the tower for air quality monitoring

visit.trail_note: Reached by the Laurel Falls Trail and Cove Mountain Trail; the tower itself is closed to hikers

events.note: Built by the CCC as a 60-ft steel Aermotor tower
Registered March 19, 2007; nominated by Peter Barr

evidence.supports: built by the CCC in 1935 in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park
evidence.quote: The Cove Mountain Fire Tower in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park was constructed by the CCC in 1935.

evidence.supports: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab
evidence.quote: It is a 60’ steel Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab.

evidence.supports: now used as an air quality monitoring site
evidence.quote: It is now used as an air quality monitoring site.

evidence.supports: built 1935; once a fire watch tower; no longer used for forest fire monitoring
evidence.quote: The 60-foot tower, built in 1935, and one of only four towers remaining in Great Smoky Mountains National Park, is no longer used for monitoring forest fire threats.

evidence.supports: National Park Service converted it into an air quality monitoring station
evidence.quote: Instead, the National Park Service has transformed it into an air quality monitoring station.

evidence.supports: hikers are not allowed into the tower
evidence.quote: As a result, hikers aren't allowed access to the tower.

evidence.supports: Laurel Falls Trail meets Cove Mountain Trail, reaching summit on foot
evidence.quote: At 3.7 miles the Laurel Falls Trail dead ends into the Cove Mountain Trail.

evidence.supports: old fire tower sits atop Cove Mountain summit, reached on foot
evidence.quote: Hikers should turn left here and walk for another tenth-of-a-mile to reach the old fire tower that sits atop the summit of Cove Mountain.

evidence.supports: NPS air quality staff monitor the air across the park
evidence.quote: are in charge of monitoring the air at Great Smoky Mountains National Park

evidence.supports: second-level room in the tower with instruments measuring air quality and weather
evidence.quote: Here in a tiny room are humming instruments busily recording air quality and weather conditions.
Ethan recalibrates each of the instruments to ensure that they are giving accurate readings.

evidence.quote: to climb to the top 80 feet in the air

notes_for_editor: No source found for the year the tower moved to air-quality use, or for any fire-lookout staffing history. Height: the register and the hiking guide say 60 feet; an NPS profile describes the top as 80 feet in the air. Not reconciled; height_m uses the 60-ft figure. The access statement comes from an undated hiking guide, not an NPS notice, so check with the NPS before publishing. The register also lists Smoky Mountain Hiking Club and Friends of the Great Smoky Mountains as cooperators; not used. A Wikidata entry gives inception 1935; not used.
